text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz has been invited by Romanian President Emil Constantinescu to visit Transylvania with him, possibly in the first half of this year.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will be unable to address the opening of Parliament's spring session today, due to an attack of influenza.
- Partliament is set to start its spring session today with a general debate on bills on protected art monuments and on child protection.
- Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima said Friday at a meeting with Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs that he supports Hungary's planned accession to the EU. (Sat.)
- The vice president of the Left-Wing Group within the Socialist Party lashed out against what he called the neo-liberal economic policy pursued by the government, and said there is an alternative.
- Sandor Lezsak, president of the Democratic Forum, plans to launch an organisation grouping regional Christian and conservative parties in April.
- State broadcaster Antenna Hungaria's equity will be raised by HUF 2.5 billion.
- Mezobank closed last year with pre-tax profits of HUF 840 million.
- The wife and daughter of the owner of a Chinese restaurant were killed early Friday when a grenade went off in a restaurant washroom shortly after closing time. (Sat.)
NEPSZABADSAG
- This paper warns of a potential collapse in the domestic grain market, as producers, mills and wholesalers are stuck with a corn and wheat surplus of at least 800,000 tons.
- This paper printed what it claims is a leaked draft report on the findings of the parliamentary commission investigating the Tocsik scandal. (Sat.)
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Hungarian-born US Congressman Tom Lantos called on Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Friday, but they declined to speak about the substance of their talks. (Sat.)
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- A senior IMF official has urged a faster reduction of inflation in Hungary, and has pledged assistance to that end from the Fund's experts, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said in Davos.
- The Ministry of Agriculture projects a 1-3 percent growth in agricultural production this year and foresees a deteriorating foreign trade balance.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- A total of $16 billion foreign capital had been invested into Hungary by the end of last year, according to the Privatisation Research Institute. Germany is the largest investor.

- A total of 6.7 million hectolitres of beer were sold in Hungary last year, as compared to 7.3 million hectolitres in 1995 and 9.8 million in 1989, Hungarian Beer Producers Association head Alan Richards said on Friday attributing the decline to the high taxes on beer.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The porcelain concern Herendi has set up a joint venture named Herend (Asia) Pte. Ltd. to market its products in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Brunei.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
